general.title: Pound Hits One-Year Low as Traders Pare BOE Rate-Hike Wagers
general.summary: The pound fell to its weakest level in almost a year against the dollar, extending declines after Wednesday’s UK inflation data prompted traders to trim bets that the Bank of England will raise interest rates.

general.title: Interest-Rates are 'Normal for Longer,' Not Higher, Says Ed Yardeni
general.summary: Fed officials left rates steady last month after raising their benchmark rate in September for the first time in three years. Since the last meeting, officials have signaled broad agreement over additional hikes, but offered differing views on the appropriate pace. Ed Yardeni, Founder of Yardeni Research, discusses the markets and his interest-rate outlook. (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: Warsh Is Closer to Waller on Fed Policy, Gopinath Says
general.summary: Gita Gopinath, former IMF deputy managing director, says Fed Chair Kevin Warsh has to "walk the talk" when it comes to bringing inflation down to its target of 2%. She says Warsh is closer to Fed Governor Christopher Waller on monetary policy. Waller is calling for a half-point hike in December. (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: Chicago’s Third CFO This Year Saw Budget Red Flags Before Exit
general.summary: The sudden departure of Chicago’s third chief financial officer in a year came after she repeatedly raised concerns about budgeting practices, including inconsistent deficit calculations.

general.title: Viral Patel on AI’s Investment Boom
general.summary: Viral Patel. the CEO of Blackstone’s private equity fund BXPE says AI demand is accelerating, not slowing, as companies ramp up adoption. He sees the biggest investment opportunity in AI infrastructure and computing, where supply may lag demand for years. Patel also points to private-market exits, selective investing, and opportunities beyond AI. Blackstone is a large investor in Anthropic. (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: BOE’s Bailey Says More Rate Hikes Needed if Iran Conflict Lasts
general.summary: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said more rate hikes will be needed the longer the conflict in the Middle East goes on, despite signs that inflation may peak below the central bank’s recent forecast of about 5%.
